prompt: Three thin blank sheets of printing paper drifting on the open sea, carried by the current, lying flat on the water as lightly as fallen leaves, seen from slightly above. The whole picture is an engraving: the sea and the sheets are both drawn in engraved steel line work, like a plate from an antique sea chart. Composition: all three sheets sit inside the upper two thirds of the image, from the centre towards the right, far apart, never touching, never overlapping, each one turned at its own angle to the current. The farthest sheet is the smallest, high on the right; the middle one a little larger; the nearest one the largest, about one fifth of the image width, at the centre-right, its lower edge still well above the bottom third. The bottom third of the image is only calm open water: long quiet engraved wave lines and nothing else, no sheet, no ripple rings, no wake, no object of any kind. The left third is calm open water too. Each sheet is a single landscape sheet of thin paper, about 3:2, wider than tall, a clear four-cornered quadrilateral with straight edges and four visible corners, lying flat on the water and gently foreshortened. Paper-thin, with no visible thickness at its edges, never a slab, never a board, never a block. Each sheet has a narrow off-white #fbfcfd paper margin and, inside it, one large blank panel bounded by a thin crisp ink grey line. The panel is one plain uniform flat light off-white tone, completely empty and flat: nothing drawn inside it, no picture, no pattern, no hatching, no shading, no wave lines, no reflection, no fold, and nothing lying across it. The panel stays dry and fully visible from corner to corner. The outer edges of the paper are wet, slightly darker where they touch the water. On one sheet only, the middle one, a single corner of the margin curls up very slightly; the other sheets are perfectly flat. One small saturated violet #7C5CD6 paper clip is clipped on the margin of the nearest sheet, at its top edge, outside the blank panel; it is the only violet in the whole image, and the margins of all three sheets are plain off-white. The sheets are drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art, their edges a single fine ink line. The water reacts to every sheet: a thin off-white foam line where the paper meets the water, a few small engraved ripples close around its edges, a short narrow wake of fine curved lines trailing behind it towards the upper right where it came from, and a darker reflection drawn in denser line hatching just beside its lower edge. Long gentle current lines flow across the sea from the upper right towards the centre. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No photographic rendering, no realistic water, no glow, no gradient, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, engraved water filling the whole image edge to edge, the sheets small in the upper two thirds from the centre to the right, open calm water on the left third and across the whole bottom third. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and saturated violet #7C5CD6 on the paper clip only.
